about: SQL Tools' PostgreSQL checks (run through psql). sources: the pages the comparisons follow; basis says whether the page text was read or only an excerpt of it. requirements: what Veeam's pages require of the configuration database account; a role attribute with no entry here is reported as a fact without a pass or fail. authentication: how the Veeam installer sets up Windows (SSPI) login. configuration_database: the name and port Veeam uses unless told otherwise; the name in use is read from the Veeam registry when this is the backup server. notes: sentences shown beside the facts they explain. queries: the named read-only queries the Read-only query offers; each is one SELECT.

requirements.label: Superuser
requirements.text: The account used for installation, upgrade and operation requires the superuser role.

notes.text: A PostgreSQL instance set up by the Veeam installer uses Windows (SSPI) authentication. pg_ident.conf maps NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and the Windows account that ran the installer to the postgres role, and postgres has a blank password in that case. Any other Windows account is refused until it is added to pg_ident.conf.
The instance the Veeam installer sets up for Backup & Replication listens on localhost only.

queries.name: Version and start time
queries.sql: SELECT version() AS version, pg_postmaster_start_time()::text AS started, (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'data_directory') AS data_directory

queries.name: Databases
queries.sql: SELECT d.datname, pg_get_userbyid(d.datdba) AS owner, pg_encoding_to_char(d.encoding) AS encoding, d.datcollate, pg_database_size(d.oid) AS size_bytes, d.datallowconn FROM pg_database d WHERE has_database_privilege(d.oid, 'CONNECT') ORDER BY d.datname

queries.name: Roles
queries.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreatedb, rolcreaterole, rolcanlogin, rolreplication, rolconnlimit, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles ORDER BY rolname

queries.name: Sessions
queries.sql: SELECT pid, usename, application_name, client_addr::text AS client_addr, state, wait_event_type, wait_event, backend_start::text AS backend_start, left(query, 200) AS query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid() ORDER BY backend_start

queries.name: Replication
queries.sql: SELECT application_name, client_addr::text AS client_addr, state, sync_state, sent_lsn::text AS sent_lsn, replay_lsn::text AS replay_lsn, replay_lag::text AS replay_lag FROM pg_stat_replication ORDER BY application_name

queries.name: WAL archiver
queries.sql: SELECT archived_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time::text AS last_archived_time, failed_count, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time::text AS last_failed_time FROM pg_stat_archiver

queries.name: Backup readiness (WAL archiving and slots)
queries.sql: SELECT current_setting('wal_level') AS wal_level, current_setting('archive_mode') AS archive_mode, CASE WHEN current_setting('archive_command') = '' THEN '(none)' ELSE current_setting('archive_command') END AS archive_command, a.archived_count, a.last_archived_wal, a.last_archived_time::text AS last_archived_time, a.failed_count, a.last_failed_wal, a.last_failed_time::text AS last_failed_time, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_stat_progress_basebackup) AS base_backups_running, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_replication_slots) AS replication_slots, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE NOT active) AS inactive_slots, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), COALESCE((SELECT MIN(restart_lsn) FROM pg_replication_slots), pg_current_wal_lsn()))) AS wal_held_by_slots FROM pg_stat_archiver AS a

queries.name: Settings changed from the default
queries.sql: SELECT name, setting, unit, source FROM pg_settings WHERE source NOT IN ('default', 'override') ORDER BY name

queries.name: Largest tables in the connected database
queries.sql: SELECT schemaname, relname, pg_total_relation_size(relid) AS total_bytes, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_autovacuum::text AS last_autovacuum FROM pg_stat_user_tables ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC LIMIT 50
